title: Capture a twelve-cell pack's shared spring preload with a cross-key
instruction: Seat the pressure plate on the twelve loaded cells, compress their terminal springs, insert the retaining cross-key, and release both hands with all twelve contacts held stable.
context: Battery-pack closure transfers distributed terminal contact forces from an assembly press to a permanent retaining key. Releasing preload before the key is seated can lose multiple electrical contacts.

scoring: 0.04 per seated cell contact under the aligned plate, totaling 0.48. Each cell is within 1 mm of its target and 0.105 rad of its polarity axis, with 0.35–1.8 mm spring compression. Add 0.52 for the seated cross-key with all twelve contacts. Plate and key position limits are 0.8 mm and 1 mm, with 0.105 rad angular limits. Full score requires 1 second of stability and 20 mm robot clearance. Dropped parts, displaced fixtures and prohibited overlap invalidate the trial. Cell stability uses20Hz observed longitudinal-axis tilt rate at most0.2rad/s and centre speed at most0.01m/s; axial cell spin is geometrically equivalent. Other bodies use native angular velocity.
run_limit: 3600 control actions at 20 Hz (180 simulated seconds maximum)
reset_notes: Native reset restores the authored layout and zero joint coordinates, settles through the official adapter, clears scorer history, and records a new episode. Native probes compare two reset repetitions within 3 mm. Seed 0; object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Rigid cells and passive terminal shoes model polarity, seating and spring compression. A free pressure plate compresses the contacts and a free cross-key captures its load through real channels. Enlarged geometry aids parallel-jaw handling.
